title: Ingress sampling mismatch + trace dead-lettering caused silent request drops during capacity spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2025-01-27 the Console experienced a class of silent failures where a subset of tenant requests were dropped without visible errors in dashboarding or alerts. Investigation revealed two blind spots: (1) inconsistent trace sampling configuration between the edge ingress & backend services leading to traces being dead-lettered and unavailable for root-cause analysis, and (2) an uninstrumented metric path for the internal ingress circuit that drops requests when queue time > 500ms (these drops were not exposed to dashboards because the metric name changed in a refactor). Without traces or the metric, on-call could not correlate spikes to KV-cache evictions and autoscaler throttling, delaying mitigation by ~45 minutes.
timeline: 2025-01-27 14:12 UTC: Console latency spike detected by synthetic checks (elevated p95).
2025-01-27 14:20 UTC: First on-call pager for increased error budget (raw errors small, but throughput dropped).
2025-01-27 15:05 UTC: Manual mitigation - increase ingress worker pool and enable emergency bypass for slow-path routing.
2025-01-27 15:50 UTC: Postmortem investigation begins; observe missing traces and an unexpected zero-rate for metric 'console.ingress.request_dropped.v2' in dashboards.
root_cause: Two simultaneous factors: (A) sampling policy mismatch — the edge sampler was configured to 1% for high QPS tenants while downstream services used adaptive sampling that rejected or dropped spans without queued buffering, causing many traces to be lost. (B) A refactor in late 2024 renamed the critical drop counter metric from 'console.ingress.request_dropped' to 'console.ingress.request_dropped.v2' but dashboards and alerts still pointed at the old name, leaving the drop signal invisible.
impact: Approximately 12% throughput degradation for affected tenants over a 40-minute window, increased latency for Console UI flows, delayed incident response because traces and drop metrics were not available to SREs. Two paying customers submitted support tickets; SLA impact was mitigated by autoscaler fallback but we missed our p99 latency SLO for Console routes during the window.
investigation_notes: Edge sampling policy file (config-edge.yaml) vs backend adaptive sampler (sampler-config): divergence confirmed; no automated validation existed for sampling contract across services.

Trace ingestion service returned 5xx for some span batches due to header-size-based rejection when a custom tenant header was present at scale. These rejections were not surfaced as metrics to the Console team.
Dashboards in Grafana referenced the old metric name; the metric still existed under new name but no translation layer or static alias was created during the refactor PR (PR #6523).
actions: A1: Add a sampling contract test in CI that validates edge and backend sampling configs are compatible (owner: Diego Moreno, estimate: 3).

A2: Add a transparent alias metric 'console.ingress.request_dropped.alias' that forwards both legacy and v2 counters for 90 days and update all dashboards/alerts to point to the alias (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 2).
A3: Instrument trace ingestion rejections as a high-cardinality metric (trace.ingest.rejected_by_header) and wire to Console observability dashboards and Alerting (owner: Lawrence Kim, estimate: 3).
A4: Update runbook and playbook to include 'missing trace/metric’ checks and a checklist to validate metric names after refactors (owner: SRE team, estimate: 1).
A5: Implement a short-term emergency probe that emits a 'round-trip trace check' from edge -> backend every 30s per region to detect orphans (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 2).
A6: Retro: schedule a quarterly telemetry-contract review between console, edge, and tracing teams; include a shared contract doc in the repo (owner: Product Engineering, estimate: 1).
acceptance_criteria: CI sampling contract test passes in the pipeline and blocks merges when sampling mismatch is detected.
Alias metric exists and dashboards/alerts are migrated; historical dashboards show continuity for last 30 days.
Trace ingestion rejection metric surfaces with an alert (rate > 0.1% sustained) and linked runbook steps.
Round-trip trace probe reports per-region success rate >= 99.9% over 24h in staging before rollout to prod.
comments: 2025-01-29 Diego Moreno: Created initial diagnostics and a repro harness for header-size rejections; see branch feature/trace-header-repro.
2025-02-03 Priya Singh: Scheduled dashboard migration for 2025-02-10; will create alias metric and deploy to staging first.
2025-02-06 Lawrence Kim: Instrumentation PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracing/pull/507 (adds trace.ingest.rejected_by_header).
2025-02-11 Aisha Patel: Round-trip probe prototype validated in staging (p95 latency 120ms, no orphans in 48h). Preparing rollout plan for canary region US-WEST1.
